 San Jose Earthquakes vs. Houston Dynamo: 5 biggest storylines for Western Conference Round One
 Justin Ruderman
 Copy URL 
 Share on Facebook 
 Share on X 
 The San Jose Earthquakes (No. 4) and Houston Dynamo FC (No. 5) square off in the Audi 2026 MLS Cup Playoffs, with Game 1 of their Round One Best-of-3 Series set for Tuesday night (10 pm ET | Apple TV ).
 Here are five key storylines to watch as Timo Werner and the Quakes clash with the Guilherme -led Dynamo in the Western Conference. 
 The series winner will meet Vancouver Whitecaps FC (No. 1) or the Wild Card winner (No. 8/9) in the Western Conference Semifinals, moving one step closer to MLS Cup presented by Audi on Dec. 18.
⚽🏆 ALL FOR THE CUP 
 Every match matters. Don't miss a moment of the Audi 2026 MLS Cup Playoffs.
 Watch on Apple TV 
 1
 San Jose's revamped attack
 When star winger Cristian Espinoza left in free agency ahead of the season and forward Cristian "Chicho" Arango was loaned out, you couldn't be blamed for thinking a regression was in store for San Jose's attack.
 However, legendary head coach Bruce Arena knew differently, handing the keys to homegrown playmaker Niko Tsakiris and making a transfer-market splash by signing UEFA Champions League winner Timo Werner.
 The plan worked perfectly as Tsakiris, despite injuries, led the team with 13 assists in a breakout season and helped striker  Preston Judd net a career-high 17 goals. Werner, for his part, added 6g/11a in his debut season, while former SuperDraft picks  Beau Leroux (4g/9a) and Ousseni Bouda (7g/4a) also made their impact felt.
 To reinforce the team in the summer window, San Jose acquired midfielder  Eduard Löwen as their newest Designated Player in a trade with St. Louis CITY SC . He's since been named a finalist for Comeback Player of the Year.
 a work of art, courtesy of @Nikotsakiris30 🖼️ pic.twitter.com/KhiXCpTb4w 
— San Jose Earthquakes (@SJEarthquakes) November 16, 2026 
 2
 Guilherme's historic campaign
 Nobody in Houston Dynamo history has recorded as many goal contributions (26; 16g/10a) in a regular-season campaign as Guilherme did in 2026.
 Arriving as one of two marquee DP signings in the offseason alongside former LAFC attacker Mateusz Bogusz , the Brazilian forward has taken the league by storm in his debut season, contributing to more than 60% of Houston's 43 goals this year.
 He's become the first Dynamo player to be a Newcomer of the Year nominee, the third player in club history to be nominated for Landon Donovan MLS MVP, and the first to earn nominations for two major, performance-based awards.
 Guilherme now has the opportunity to further rewrite the record books as he makes his MLS Cup Playoffs debut.
 3
 PayPal Park's playoff debut
 Opened more than a decade ago, San Jose's PayPal Park will finally host its first playoff game on Nov. 24.
 That's because San Jose have reached the postseason just three times since 2013, finishing no higher than sixth and falling in their opening playoff game away from home on each occasion.
 But that's all changed under Arena, the winningest coach in MLS history who led the Quakes to their first top-four finish since lifting the 2012 Supporters' Shield.
 Already a record five-time MLS Cup champion with D.C. United and the LA Galaxy , Arena is seeking a sixth title with a third MLS original club in 2026.
 READY FOR IMPACT ⚠️ @prestonjudd10 on the home crowd, the @PayPalPark energy, and getting ready for the moment.
the grit reaper is ready to get to work 🏴‍☠️
BRACE FOR IMPACT ⚠️ presented by @useapolloio pic.twitter.com/jwbNx6x9Zb 
— San Jose Earthquakes (@SJEarthquakes) November 17, 2026 
 4
 Houston's (previous) playoff pedigree
 Only three teams have won back-to-back MLS Cup titles, including the 2006-07 Houston Dynamo.
 The Dynamo also reached MLS Cup in 2011 and 2012, falling to the LA Galaxy in both finals.
 Fast forward nearly 15 years and Houston are trying to reclaim their glory days. They've already won the 2023 US Open Cup under head coach Ben Olsen, and now could tie Columbus Crew (3) for the third-most titles in league history.
 5
 San Jose's (previous) playoff pedigree
 Beginning with their 2001 MLS Cup title, San Jose arguably became a dynasty.
 From 2001-05, the Quakes won two MLS Cup titles and a Supporters' Shield. They finished below second in the West just once.
 But since 2008, San Jose have qualified for the playoffs just six times, claiming one trophy (2012 Supporters' Shield) and winning one playoff series.
 Now, they have home-field advantage for the first time since 2012 and hope to prove they're officially back.
